🔍 Master PySpark Faster with This Visual Cheatsheet! 💡

Working with big data often means dealing with massive volumes of distributed data — and PySpark is one of the most powerful tools to get the job done efficiently. Whether you're transforming terabytes of logs, cleaning messy datasets, or running complex aggregations, PySpark’s DataFrame API is your go-to toolkit.

But let's be honest — keeping track of every function’s syntax isn't always easy. So, I created this visual cheatsheet highlighting some of the most frequently used PySpark functions 🚀

📊 What's Inside the Cheatsheet:
✔️ select() – Choose specific columns from a DataFrame
 ✔️ filter() – Filter rows based on conditions
 ✔️ groupBy().count() – Aggregate data efficiently
 ✔️ agg() – Perform advanced aggregations like avg, sum, max
 ✔️ join() – Combine multiple datasets based on keys
 ✔️ orderBy() – Sort data
 ✔️ distinct() – Remove duplicates
 ✔️ drop() – Remove columns
 ✔️ withColumn() – Create or modify columns
 ✔️ replace() – Handle missing or invalid values
 ✔️ isNull() – Identify missing values
 ✔️ sample() – Random sampling of your data

🛠️ Why It’s Useful:
✅ Speeds up development by giving you quick syntax references
 ✅ Helps you transition from Pandas or SQL into PySpark smoothly
 ✅ Ideal for interviews, notebooks, and project kickstarts
 ✅ Great for both beginners and seasoned Spark users


🔄 Feel free to save, share, or repost this with your network. Let’s make big data work easier for everyone!
